comments.text:
So off topic, but the body in a freezer reminds me of this time in 7th grade when I took a middle school friend of mine to a family reunion at a farm in Iowa. They had us stay in a loft which was above this garage they had detached from the house . They didnt keep cars in the garage, it was more of a hang out space/ rec room for the kids (they had even built a functional kitchen at the back of it). Anyway, my friend got up in the middle of the night to grab a snack and in the kitchen found 2 fridges. One fridge, did indeed have snacks and pastries to which she helped herself to. So she opened up the second fridge to see if there were more and found instead… meat. A lot of it. And some of it still with the blood frozen around the packaging. I remember her shriek waking me in the night to this day, and her panic as she told me my aunt and uncle (whose house we were at) must have murdered someone.
They in fact were not murderers, but instead had recently sent an old cow of theirs to slaughter, and not wanting to put anything to waste, were saving the cow’s meat for meals throughout the winter. 
Needless to say it was a very sleepless night for my friend though

comments.text:
For those who don't understand this yet, the cycle of abuse includes a cycle of leaving & returning, & the fact that many VICTIMS, break it off but then go back, is not evidence that the women are foolish, or naive, or too hopeful. The men deliberately behave in a manipulative way, & most importantly, so many men behave that way, but we really only hear about the men who murder the woman. My own daughter, in her 30's, with kids, just finally kicked her husband out. 

The best illustration of what I'm talking about is that they were together for 6 years, but she'd thrown him out twice before, earlier in the relationship. But he vowed to be better, & was for a while, but when his own arrogance cost him his job, & he refused to listen to any of us about how to start his own business, it failed, & he started playing video games more & more. He spiraled into serious abuse, they would fight, she'd be ready to throw him out, he'd admit fault, apologize, promise to be better, cycle repeats. 

Until finally, they go to therapy together, & in the very first session, he admitted that every single time he admiited fault, he was just annoyed with her being such a crazy person, so to make that stop, he'd fake it for a while. That really exposed who he was, & convinced her that she needed to let the idea of being together go. She allowed him to stay in her home for 2 more weeks while he finally worked to raise money, & he put her thru hell. He cycled thru trying to convince her to have sex, to trying to manipulate her by showing her the various cards he'd given her over time, & when that didn't work, he'd berate her for hours by text.

The problem isn't women, it us men. Even the most decent men I know, don't want to discuss this, & they make those common comments, which just prevents change in the long run.
